conventions: The phrase 'be-eynei' plus suffix is read two ways in this chapter, and the difference is the ASV's word count rather than a split. At 1SA.1.18 the ASV writes 'in thy sight' - a word for the preposition, a word for the noun, a word for the suffix - so rule 30's one-rendering condition is unmet and rule 2 splits all three. At 1SA.1.23 the ASV writes 'what seemeth thee good', spending one English word on the preposition and its construct noun together, so those two share one unit headed on the verb, on the model of rule 40's 'im-ra be-eyneykha' to 'if it displease thee'. The predicate adjective tov is not drawn into that fusion, because it holds its own 'good' and rule 30's subtraction test finds a word spent on it in particular; the suffix keeps the 'thee' rule 18 writes for it. The competing reading, which takes 'seemeth' as rule 20's linking copula joining tov and marks both preposition and noun unrepresented, is named in the 1SA.1.23 unit note.

'ad matay' rendered 'How long' with no matrix frame written is split morpheme by morpheme, as rule 17's closing sentence directs: the temporal interrogative matay takes 'How', which writes its wh-lexeme, and 'ad takes 'long', which is the extent the preposition states. This is not rule 17's indivisible 'how long will it be ere' unit, which that rule reserves for a clause carrying a separate English matrix frame; here the ASV writes only the question itself, so nothing is fused.

'kol ha-yamim asher hayah' rendered 'as long as he liveth' divides as follows: kol and yamim share the fused 'as long', headed on yamim as the morpheme carrying the lexeme; the separately segmented article is its own unrepresented unit, following rule 30's ruling on 'divrei ha-yamim' to 'chronicles'; asher takes the second 'as'; and hayah keeps 'he liveth'. Note for a later reader that the corpus carries seven units of kol plus article plus yamim as one noncompositional 'for ever' headed on 'ever', with the article inside the fusion. That is a different status under rule 6 and does not govern an 'aligned' fusion, which rule 30 expressly directs the article out of; the divergence is recorded here rather than silently reconciled.
report: Read all 28 verses end to end against the candidate table, the validation report and the corpus rows. No construction is analysed two ways with nothing in the source or in the ASV to license the difference. Verdict no-change, patches empty.

Waw (87 occurrences, the largest bucket): every treatment is a connective the ASV actually wrote, which rule 14's open list permits. The two unrepresented waws are real rather than oversights - 1SA.1.4 s008, where the ASV writes no connective before 'he gave', and 1SA.1.15 s013, the clause-initial waw, where 'neither' goes to the present negative and 'nor' to the coordinating waw under rule 14's correlative carve-out.

Preposition lamed (29 occurrences): every unrepresented one is a recasting that writes no function word. The two possessive clauses of 1SA.1.2 put 'had' on hayah and 'had no' on ayin under rule 43; the gerund infinitives of 1SA.1.12 and 1SA.1.26 write nothing for it under rule 52; 1SA.1.27 has a bare English indirect object, 1SA.1.28 a bare object, and 1SA.1.18 an ethical dative whose suffix is unrendered as well (rule 40). Wherever a word is written the lamed takes it.

Article (24 occurrences): the unrepresented ones are an article on a toponym for which the ASV writes no 'the' (1SA.1.1, 1SA.1.19, rule 29); an article whose single written determiner another morpheme holds (1SA.1.3 and 1SA.1.27, where the demonstrative pronoun takes it under rules 41 and 47); and the article inside the fused expression of 1SA.1.28 (rule 30). 1SA.1.9's article to 'his' is rule 41's possessive determiner with no suffix standing in the phrase, and the corpus carries 32 such units.

The one candidate that looked like a genuine split is not one. 1SA.1.18 renders preposition-plus-eyn-plus-suffix as 'in thy sight', one English word per morpheme, so rule 2 splits it; 1SA.1.23 renders the same phrase as 'seemeth' inside 'what seemeth thee good', one English word for the preposition and its construct noun together, so rule 30 fuses them while tov stays outside the fusion holding its own 'good'. What differs is the ASV's word count, which is exactly the condition rule 30 states. Recorded as a convention.

The five 'added' units, which the lemma-keyed table cannot see, run one consistent count across the chapter. 1SA.1.4's supplied 'when' stands over a temporal clause with no morpheme in it and a waw already holding 'And'; the same count comes out the other way in 1SA.1.12, where ki takes 'as', and in 1SA.1.20, where the temporal lamed takes 'when'. The apodosis waw takes the frame's 'that' in all three (rule 45). The remaining three are 1SA.1.7's italic 'as' beside two ken each holding a written 'so', 1SA.1.18's supplied predicate 'sad', and 1SA.1.20's supplied 'saying'; 1SA.1.22's italic clause is one added unit under rule 2.

Construct chains are uniform: the construct takes a supplied 'the' (1SA.1.1 four times, 1SA.1.2, 1SA.1.7, 1SA.1.11, 1SA.1.16, 1SA.1.17, 1SA.1.24), and where an article morpheme stands on the rectum that morpheme takes the written 'the' instead (1SA.1.2, 1SA.1.20, 1SA.1.21). Supplied prepositions before bare nominals go to the noun throughout (1SA.1.10, 1SA.1.15, 1SA.1.24 three times, rule 33), and 1SA.1.10 and 1SA.1.15 agree in principle: the outer supplied preposition goes to the word opening the phrase, and the inner relation to the rectum only where the ASV writes one.

BSB: no genuine error. The Td x 7 and R x 9 blocks are the documented convention differences (rules 29, 40, 43, 52). The single-token candidates are settled by rule: the object marker at 1SA.1.21 by rule 16, the paragogic nun at 1SA.1.14 by rule 32, and the two waws named above by rule 14. The remaining two, achat at 1SA.1.5 and gam at 1SA.1.6, are judgment calls whose competing readings are already named in the unit notes; neither is an error and neither should be changed to raise the agreement rate.

One tension worth flagging rather than legislating: 1SA.1.28 fuses kol with yamim as 'as long' and leaves the article its own unrepresented unit, following rule 30's explicit ruling on divrei ha-yamim to 'chronicles'. The corpus instead carries seven kol + article + yamim units as noncompositional 'for ever' with the article inside the fusion. The chapter followed the contract's own text, so I left it and recorded the divergence as a convention rather than promoting a rule the corpus would contradict.
